N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 is used for post-exposure functional testing; chemical exposure needs the specified facility/fluids/safety controls.

Purpose / failure mechanism: Handling drops can crack ceramics/ferrites or detach components without visible external damage Cross-reference: For components inside an electric-propulsion system, ISO 19453-3/-4/-5 may govern instead of ISO 16750-3/-4/-5.
Typical stimulus / conditions: Drop per standard (height and orientation per spec), then functional test and inspection
Measure / record: Function, visible and hidden damage (X-ray if needed)
Acceptance / target: No hidden damage; function per requirement
Equipment required: functional electrical test bench based on N6700; Drop fixture; X-ray for analysis
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 performs pre/post electrical checks; add a drop fixture, with X-ray optional for hidden-damage analysis.

Purpose / failure mechanism: Altitude reduces convective cooling and simultaneously reduces the withstand of clearances, so both derate together. A design verified at sea level can fail thermally and electrically at altitude. Neither TH-001 nor AUTO-020 covers it Cross-reference: For components inside an electric-propulsion system, ISO 19453-3/-4/-5 may govern instead of ISO 16750-3/-4/-5.
Typical stimulus / conditions: Operate at full load at the specified reduced pressure and elevated temperature; repeat dielectric withstand at reduced pressure where the barrier relies on clearance rather than solid insulation
Measure / record: Case and component temperatures against the sea-level baseline; thermal-derating shift; breakdown or flashover at reduced pressure
Acceptance / target: Meets thermal derating and dielectric requirements at the specified maximum operating altitude
Equipment required: Altitude/low-pressure chamber, ideally combined with temperature; dielectric-withstand capability inside the chamber for the electrical part
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads if feed-throughs exist; the pressure chamber is external
Main reference: IEC 60068-2-13; IEC 60664-1 altitude correction; confirm whether the customer specification or the ISO 16750-4 edition in force imposes a level

Test: 48 V supply voltage range and slow transients
Purpose / failure mechanism: Validate components connected to nominal 48 V vehicle electrical system
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply defined 48 V ranges, slow transients/fluctuations and operating modes
Measure / record: output voltage, input current, state, protection
Acceptance / target: Meets ISO/customer functional requirements
Equipment required: N6775A source for profile portions at or below 60 volts; N6791A electronic load where load power is at or below 100 watts; digital oscilloscope; thermal chamber; 48 V-capable programmable source / 4-quadrant source as needed
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A covers only profile portions at or below 60 volts and 5 amperes; higher-voltage/fast/regenerative portions need another source. N6791A is limited to 100 watts.
Main reference: ISO 21780:2020 (confirmed 2026; functional status FS1–FS5); LV 148 / VDA 320

Purpose / failure mechanism: Validate DC-link-connected component against traction-system electrical behavior Cross-reference: ISO 21498-1:2021 defines the voltage sub-classes that determine which ISO 21498-2 levels apply.
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply customer/ISO-defined voltage class B profiles and operating conditions
Measure / record: Terminal V/I, function, insulation monitoring as applicable
Acceptance / target: Meets component requirement
Equipment required: high-voltage source/load, safety interlocks, isolation measurement
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A/N6791A are not primary voltage-class-B source/load equipment; use rated high-voltage source/load/probes/interlocks.
Main reference: ISO 21498-2:2024 (electrical safety excluded, see HV-002); LV 123 / VW 80300

Purpose / failure mechanism: Electrical-safety functions of HV-connected converters, outside the scope of ISO 21498-2
Typical stimulus / conditions: Insulation resistance HV↔LV/chassis; active and passive discharge timing; high-voltage interlock response
Measure / record: Insulation resistance, discharge time to safe voltage, interlock reaction
Acceptance / target: Meets ISO 6469-3 and vehicle-manufacturer requirements
Equipment required: high-voltage insulation tester, high-voltage source, safety interlocks
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 cannot replace high-voltage insulation/discharge/interlock safety equipment; it may power auxiliary low-voltage circuits.

Purpose / failure mechanism: AUTO-019 and AUTO-020 are one-shot pass/fail tests. For a barrier switching at tens of kilohertz with fast edges, the wear-out mechanism is partial discharge in voids inside the insulation system, which a dielectric-withstand test passes without detecting
Typical stimulus / conditions: Derive required clearance, creepage and impulse withstand from working voltage, overvoltage category and pollution degree; then measure partial-discharge inception and extinction voltage across the barrier, before and after humidity and temperature-cycling stress
Measure / record: Measured clearance and creepage; impulse-withstand result; partial discharge inception and extinction voltage; drift after stress
Acceptance / target: Coordination satisfied with margin; partial discharge extinction voltage above the maximum working voltage across the barrier, including after environmental stress
Equipment required: Partial-discharge test set; impulse generator; mechanical clearance measurement; safety enclosure
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 has no role. Specialised HV insulation equipment and a safety enclosure are required
Main reference: IEC 60664-1; IEC 62477-1; SAE 2013-01-1528; extends AUTO-019 and AUTO-020

Test: Common-mode transient immunity across the isolation barrier
Purpose / failure mechanism: An isolated converter's feedback, gate-drive and communication paths cross the barrier and see the full common-mode dV/dt of the HV switching node. Insufficient common-mode transient immunity appears as data corruption, false shutdown or duty-cycle disturbance rather than as a barrier failure, so HV-003 will not find it
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply defined common-mode dV/dt steps across the barrier at the worst-case rate the application produces; sweep operating point and temperature
Measure / record: Bit errors, feedback disturbance, false fault assertions, output disturbance during the transient
Acceptance / target: No functional upset at the maximum dV/dt the application can produce, with the margin required by the component datasheet
Equipment required: Common-mode transient generator or representative switching fixture; isolated high-bandwidth probing; differential probes
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads; the common-mode stimulus and isolated probing are external
Main reference: Isolator and gate-driver datasheet common-mode transient immunity ratings; product requirement; complements HV-003

Test: AC input voltage and frequency operating range
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify an on-board charger across the declared external AC supply envelope and identify transfer, derating and shutdown boundaries
Typical stimulus / conditions: Sweep rated single-phase or three-phase input voltage and frequency over the project range at light, nominal and full charging power and temperature corners
Measure / record: AC voltage/current/power, power factor, DC-link/HV output, charge power, state and faults
Acceptance / target: Charging function and protection remain within the product, market and vehicle requirements throughout the declared range
Equipment required: Programmable AC/grid simulator; HV battery simulator or regenerative DC load; precision power analyzer; isolation and safety interlocks; thermal chamber
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can power low-voltage auxiliaries and controls only. It cannot emulate the mains input or traction-battery power path of a normal OBC.
Main reference: ISO 5474-1:2024; ISO 5474-2:2024; IEC 61851-21-1:2017; product and market requirements

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify controlled charging behavior through reduced mains voltage without undefined state, unsafe current or corrupted charging control
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply project/market voltage dips and reduced-voltage plateaus at several phase angles, loads and temperatures; include repeated dips near the charger dropout boundary
Measure / record: Input current, charge power, DC output, state transitions, diagnostics and recovery
Acceptance / target: Required charging state is maintained or exited deterministically; no unsafe current, latch-up or undefined recovery
Equipment required: Programmable AC/grid simulator with dip capability; HV battery simulator/load; oscilloscope; power analyzer
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 may support auxiliary rails and monitoring, but the AC disturbance requires a grid simulator or compliant immunity generator.
Main reference: ISO 5474-2:2024; IEC 61000-4-11:2020 and IEC 61000-4-34 where applicable; vehicle/market requirement

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify deterministic behavior and recovery after complete loss of external AC during charging
Typical stimulus / conditions: Interrupt one or all AC conductors for the required durations at multiple charging powers and phases of operation; restore the source with controlled phase and voltage
Measure / record: Hold-up, contactor state, DC-link decay, charge termination, restart delay, diagnostics and communication state
Acceptance / target: No unsafe energy transfer or contactor state; restart/recovery follows the specified sequence without corrupted state
Equipment required: Programmable AC/grid simulator or synchronized contactor; HV battery simulator/load; oscilloscope; communications monitor
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can maintain low-voltage support if required, but it does not generate the AC interruption on the charger input.
Main reference: ISO 5474-1:2024; ISO 5474-2:2024; IEC 61000-4-11:2020 / IEC 61000-4-34 as applicable; product requirement

Test: Three-phase phase loss and voltage unbalance
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that a three-phase OBC detects and safely handles a missing phase, phase-voltage unbalance and phase restoration
Typical stimulus / conditions: At representative charge powers remove each phase in turn and apply specified voltage unbalance; repeat during startup and steady charging
Measure / record: Per-phase voltage/current, neutral current where applicable, DC-link ripple, output power, diagnostics and recovery
Acceptance / target: No component overstress or uncontrolled current; defined derating/shutdown and deterministic recovery
Equipment required: Three-phase programmable grid simulator with independent phase control; power analyzer; HV battery simulator/load; oscilloscope
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can power auxiliary electronics only. Independent three-phase source control is external.
Main reference: ISO 5474-2:2024; IEC 61000-4-27:2000+A1:2009+A2:2025 where applicable; product/grid requirement

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify mains-side inrush, DC-link precharge and repeated energization stress for the on-board charger
Typical stimulus / conditions: Energize at worst source voltage and phase angle with discharged and partially charged DC link; repeat hot/cold and after short off-times
Measure / record: Peak and RMS input current, charge, current-squared-time, DC-link rise, relay/contactor timing and component stress
Acceptance / target: Inrush, fuse/relay stress and precharge timing remain within design limits; no nuisance protection or welded contactor
Equipment required: Programmable AC source or synchronized mains switch; wide-band current probe; power analyzer; HV battery simulator/load; safety enclosure
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 is not the AC source. It can support auxiliary/control rails and synchronized logging only.

Test: AC input power factor and efficiency map
Purpose / failure mechanism: Characterize charger power factor, apparent power and conversion efficiency over the charging envelope
Typical stimulus / conditions: Sweep AC voltage/frequency, charge power, HV battery voltage and temperature; include single-phase and three-phase modes where supported
Measure / record: True power, apparent power, reactive power, displacement/total power factor, AC-to-DC efficiency and temperature
Acceptance / target: Meets project, market and thermal-efficiency targets over the declared operating envelope
Equipment required: Precision multi-channel power analyzer; programmable grid source; regenerative HV battery simulator/load; thermal chamber
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 may power auxiliaries but cannot substitute for the mains source, regenerative HV load or precision AC power analyzer.
Main reference: ISO 5474-2:2024; product energy-efficiency and grid-interface requirements

Test: Harmonic current and flicker on the AC charging input
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that the OBC does not inject excessive low-frequency harmonic current or objectionable voltage fluctuation into the public supply
Typical stimulus / conditions: Operate the charger in the prescribed power states and execute the applicable harmonic-current and voltage-fluctuation/flicker methods for its rated current and connection class
Measure / record: Current harmonic spectrum, total harmonic distortion, voltage changes and flicker metrics
Acceptance / target: Within the applicable public-supply limits for the charger rating and market
Equipment required: Compliant AC source/reference impedance; harmonic/flicker-capable power analyzer; HV battery simulator/load
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 has no formal role in the AC harmonic/flicker measurement other than optional auxiliary-power support.

Test: Protective-earth continuity through the vehicle charging path
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify the protective bonding path used while conductively connected to external power and detect excessive resistance or an open protective-earth path
Typical stimulus / conditions: Measure protective-bond continuity with the vehicle/OBC in the specified connection states; inject an open/high-resistance PE fault where the architecture provides monitoring
Measure / record: Bond resistance or voltage drop, PE monitor response, charge inhibit and diagnostic timing
Acceptance / target: Protective bonding and monitoring meet the applicable vehicle power-transfer safety requirement; unsafe charging is inhibited
Equipment required: Protective-bond/ground-continuity tester; charging inlet/EVSE interface fixture; HV safety enclosure
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 cannot perform the required protective-earth continuity test; it may power low-voltage controls during monitoring checks.
Main reference: ISO 5474-1:2024; ISO 5474-2:2024; ISO 6469-3:2021; applicable charging-interface requirement

Test: Leakage, isolation and residual-current behavior while charging
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that mains-to-chassis/HV leakage and isolation-monitor behavior remain safe in normal operation and relevant single-fault conditions
Typical stimulus / conditions: Measure leakage/isolation in defined charging states and inject representative insulation or leakage faults through controlled impedances; repeat across AC/HV voltage and temperature corners
Measure / record: Leakage/residual current, isolation resistance, monitor threshold and reaction time, contactor state
Acceptance / target: Within applicable shock-protection limits; faults are detected and charging is inhibited/disconnected within the specified time
Equipment required: Leakage-current measurement network; insulation-resistance tester; programmable fault impedance; grid simulator; HV battery simulator; safety interlocks
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 only supports low-voltage auxiliaries. Formal leakage/isolation testing needs dedicated mains/HV safety instrumentation.
Main reference: ISO 5474-1:2024; ISO 5474-2:2024; ISO 6469-3:2021; charging-system safety concept

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify charging current/voltage limits, contactor sequencing and protection coordination between OBC and battery-management system
Typical stimulus / conditions: Exercise requested current/voltage boundaries, battery-temperature/voltage limits, contactor delays and BMS inhibit/derating commands; inject stale, inconsistent and boundary values through supported interfaces
Measure / record: Commanded vs actual current/voltage, contactor timing, limit enforcement, diagnostics and final state
Acceptance / target: No command or timing condition can exceed battery/OBC allocated limits; inhibit and derating commands are honored within required reaction time
Equipment required: HV battery simulator or BMS emulator; vehicle communications interface; oscilloscope; fault-injection/test hooks; safety interlocks
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 may emulate low-voltage auxiliaries and some signal-level conditions, but the HV battery interface and BMS emulation are external.
Main reference: ISO 26262 safety requirements and interfaces; vehicle battery/OBC requirement; ISO 5474 power-transfer context

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that credible charger faults do not create hazardous HV/mains exposure, uncontrolled battery current or unsafe contactor state
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject representative sensor, feedback, control, cooling, contactor and power-stage faults identified by FMEA/FMEDA/DFA while charging at worst relevant operating corners
Measure / record: Fault electrical effect, detection time, protection reaction, contactor/isolation state, temperatures and recovery
Acceptance / target: Each credited safety mechanism detects the allocated fault and reaches/maintains the specified safe or degraded state within the allocated timing
Equipment required: HV grid/battery simulators; protected fault-injection fixture; isolated probes; thermal instrumentation; interlocked enclosure
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 is useful for low-voltage auxiliary fault conditions only. High-energy charger faults require dedicated protected equipment.
Main reference: ISO 26262-5/-9; ISO 5474-1:2024; ISO 5474-2:2024; ISO 6469-3:2021; project safety analysis

Test: V2G/V2H power-flow direction change and four-quadrant transition
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify safe and stable transition between grid-to-vehicle charging and vehicle-to-grid/home export modes
Typical stimulus / conditions: Command repeated direction changes at AC/HV voltage, power and temperature corners; include reversal during load/grid disturbances and near zero power
Measure / record: Transition time, AC and HV current, DC-link excursion, contactor state, cross-conduction, exported/imported power and communication state
Acceptance / target: No uncontrolled current or rail excursion; deterministic handover and protection behavior; power direction matches negotiated state
Equipment required: Regenerative four-quadrant grid simulator; regenerative HV battery simulator; multi-channel power analyzer; isolated oscilloscope probes; ISO 15118 communication stack/emulator
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 cannot provide regenerative mains/HV operation. It can support low-voltage auxiliary rails and synchronized control/monitoring.
Main reference: ISO 5474-1:2024 and ISO 5474-2:2024 reverse power transfer; ISO 15118-20:2022 bidirectional power-transfer communication; applicable grid requirements

Test: Grid loss and anti-islanding response during exported power
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that a V2G-capable vehicle stops or transitions exported power correctly when the external grid becomes unavailable or leaves allowed conditions
Typical stimulus / conditions: While exporting power, open the grid connection and apply out-of-range grid voltage/frequency conditions defined by the applicable market/interconnection rule
Measure / record: Export current and power, disconnect/transition time, contactor state, island voltage/frequency and reconnection behavior
Acceptance / target: Meets the applicable grid interconnection protection and reconnection requirements; no unintended energized island
Equipment required: Regenerative grid simulator with anti-islanding test capability or certified grid-interconnection test system; HV battery simulator; power analyzer
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 has no role in the grid-protection stimulus except auxiliary/control support.
Main reference: Applicable national grid/interconnection requirements for bidirectional EV charging; ISO 5474-1/-2 power-transfer framework; ISO 15118-20:2022 communication context

Test: Charging recovery after communication loss or invalid charging sequence
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that loss, corruption or invalid ordering of EV-EVSE charging communication cannot leave uncontrolled energy transfer or an undefined recovery state
Typical stimulus / conditions: Interrupt communication at each major charging phase; inject timeout, malformed/unsupported state and inconsistent power-limit sequences through a compliant emulator where supported
Measure / record: Power flow, contactor state, timeout/detection time, diagnostics, restart/re-authentication sequence and retained state
Acceptance / target: Energy transfer stops or transitions to the defined safe state within the required timeout; restart requires the specified valid sequence and never resumes from stale limits
Equipment required: ISO 15118/charging-communication emulator; EVSE interface; grid and HV battery simulators; oscilloscope; fault injection at communication link
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 may power auxiliary electronics and log low-voltage behavior; charging communication and high-power interfaces require dedicated emulation.
Main reference: ISO 15118-20:2022; ISO 5474-1:2024; ISO 5474-2:2024; ISO 26262 where communication loss is safety-related

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify OV/UV monitors, watchdog, safe state and the diagnostic-coverage claims of the safety concept
Typical stimulus / conditions: Fault injection: drive rails beyond monitor thresholds, open/short feedback, clock loss; measure detection and reaction
Measure / record: Detection thresholds, fault reaction time vs fault-tolerant time interval, safe-state entry, built-in self-test/latent-fault results
Acceptance / target: Meets safety requirements (thresholds, timing, coverage)
Equipment required: N6775A programmable source; N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; Fault-injection fixture, function generator
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A can inject supply over/undervoltage and N6791A load faults; internal/control faults need dedicated fault-injection hardware.
Main reference: ISO 26262-4:2018 and ISO 26262-5:2018; item/system safety concept and hardware safety requirements

Purpose / failure mechanism: Prove that regulation, monitor thresholds and the load valid-operating range retain margin across tolerance, temperature, transients and ageing
Typical stimulus / conditions: Combine worst-case regulation and transient data with measured overvoltage/undervoltage monitor thresholds, hysteresis and deglitch timing over temperature; include post-stress drift
Measure / record: Regulation extrema, transient extrema, monitor trip/release thresholds, hysteresis, deglitch time and remaining margin
Acceptance / target: Regulation including transients remains inside the monitor window, and the monitor window remains inside the safety-related load valid-operating range, with documented margin
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; thermal chamber; calibrated precision digital multimeter recommended for threshold verification
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A/N6791A reproduce the electrical corners and N6700 logs them; the oscilloscope measures threshold/deglitch timing and the chamber covers temperature corners.
Main reference: ISO 26262-5:2018 hardware safety requirements and verification; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-002

Test: Fault reaction time versus fault-tolerant time interval
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify that fault detection plus fault reaction reaches the defined safe or degraded state before the allocated fault-tolerant time interval expires
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject representative overvoltage, undervoltage, feedback and oscillation faults at worst-case temperature and timing tolerance; time-stamp fault onset, detection and safe-state completion
Measure / record: Fault-detection time interval, fault-reaction time interval, total reaction time, safe-state outputs and fault flags
Acceptance / target: Worst measured detection plus reaction time is less than or equal to the allocated fault-tolerant time interval with project-defined margin
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; thermal chamber; fault-injection fixtures/test hooks as required
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A can create programmed supply faults and N6791A loads the output; the oscilloscope provides correlated timing. Feedback/component faults require dedicated injection fixtures.
Main reference: ISO 26262-1:2018 timing definitions; ISO 26262-4:2018 technical safety concept; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-003

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify self-test or periodic-test coverage of faults in voltage monitors, references, reset paths and safe-state paths that the safety case counts as detected
Typical stimulus / conditions: Use device test modes or fault-injection hooks to force comparator, reference, reset/error-path and related latent faults; verify detection within the multiple-point fault-detection interval
Measure / record: Detection result, detection time, diagnostic flag, start inhibit or safe-state reaction
Acceptance / target: Every latent fault credited as detected by the safety analysis is detected within its allocated detection interval and causes the specified reaction
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; device test mode or dedicated fault-injection fixture; control/communications interface
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 establishes the operating point and records rail behavior; latent-fault injection normally depends on device-specific test modes or external fixtures.
Main reference: ISO 26262-5:2018 hardware architectural metrics and fault-injection verification; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-004

Purpose / failure mechanism: Show that a shared-resource fault cannot corrupt regulation and its monitoring simultaneously where independence is claimed
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject shared reference/bandgap drift, feedback-divider faults, feedback-pin shorts, monitor supply/ground faults, clock faults and local overtemperature identified by dependent-failure analysis
Measure / record: Output excursion, monitor response, diagnostic response and safe-state transition
Acceptance / target: No single identified shared-resource fault produces an undetected output excursion beyond the safety limit
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; thermal chamber; circuit-level fault-injection fixture and device test hooks
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies/loads the converter and measures rail behavior; shared-resource faults require design-specific injection access.
Main reference: ISO 26262-9:2018 dependent-failure analysis; ISO 26262-5:2018; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-005

Purpose / failure mechanism: Experimentally substantiate diagnostic-coverage claims where the failure-mode-effects-and-diagnostic analysis or safety case relies on physical detection of representative component faults
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject safe representative component failure modes such as switch short, output-capacitor open, feedback-divider open/short, current-sense drift, inductor fault and reference drift
Measure / record: Injected fault, observed electrical effect, diagnostic detection, reaction time and resulting state
Acceptance / target: Observed fault effect and detection agree with the safety analysis; update the analysis and claimed diagnostic coverage when they do not
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; relay/transistor fault-injection fixtures; configurable links or programmable fault elements; safety enclosure as needed
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 provides repeatable source/load conditions and logging; physical component-fault injection needs dedicated fixtures and protection.
Main reference: ISO 26262-5:2018 fault-injection testing and Annex D; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-006

Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify the complete path from fault detection to the defined safe state and prove that the state is held until the specified recovery condition
Typical stimulus / conditions: Trigger each safety mechanism, including with the controlling microcontroller unresponsive; verify fail-safe/error/reset outputs, downstream enables, latching, retry counters and recovery rules
Measure / record: Safe-state outputs, entry time, state retention, retry behavior and recovery condition
Acceptance / target: Safe state is reached within the allocated time, maintained as specified and exited only through the permitted recovery condition
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; fault-injection fixture; control/communications isolation fixture as required
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 reproduces electrical conditions; oscilloscope correlates fault, detection and safe-state outputs. Controller-independent path testing needs additional fixture/control.
Main reference: ISO 26262-4:2018 technical safety concept; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-007

Test: Digital safety mechanisms in power-management or system-basis devices
Purpose / failure mechanism: Verify configuration-memory integrity, serial-interface protection, watchdog, clock monitoring and built-in self-test mechanisms where present
Typical stimulus / conditions: Corrupt configuration/test registers through supported test modes; inject serial cyclic-redundancy-check/framing errors; disturb clock/watchdog timing; execute logic or analog built-in self-test as applicable
Measure / record: Diagnostic flags, error outputs, reset/safe-state reaction, detection time and recovery behavior
Acceptance / target: Each applicable digital safety mechanism detects the injected error and produces the reaction specified by the device safety manual and project safety requirement
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; communications exerciser; programmable clock/watchdog/error-injection capability; device-specific test mode
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies/loads and logs rail behavior; digital mechanism verification requires the relevant serial/control interfaces and device test features.
Main reference: ISO 26262-11:2018 semiconductor guidance; device safety manual; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-008

Purpose / failure mechanism: For fail-operational or decomposed architectures, verify switchover, fault isolation and emergency-operation duration after loss of either supply path
Typical stimulus / conditions: Fail each supply path under load using open, short-to-ground, short-to-battery and overvoltage faults; measure switchover and hold-up; verify cross-current isolation and emergency operation duration
Measure / record: Switchover time, hold-up voltage, equalizing current, isolation of faulted path and emergency-operation duration
Acceptance / target: No interruption beyond the safety requirement; faulted path is isolated and emergency operation is maintained for at least the allocated emergency-operation tolerance interval
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; additional independent source/load channels; digital oscilloscope; multi-pole fault-insertion/OR-ing fixture
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: The installed N6775A and N6791A cover one source/load path; redundant-path verification requires at least one additional independent source/load path and switching fixture.
Main reference: ISO 26262-4:2018 emergency operation; ISO 26262-9:2018 decomposition/dependent failures; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-009

Test: Expanded functional testing with rare and out-of-specification inputs
Purpose / failure mechanism: Exercise rare combinations and invalid sequences that can expose undefined safety-related behavior beyond normal qualification profiles
Typical stimulus / conditions: Combine invalid commands, enable toggling during start-up/shutdown, fault during start-up, crank plus load step, maximum temperature plus minimum input plus maximum load, and enable glitches near thresholds
Measure / record: Rail behavior, diagnostic response, reset/safe-state behavior, recovery and any undefined state
Acceptance / target: Behavior remains defined by the safety requirements; no undetected or latched unsafe state
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 modular power system with N6775A source and N6791A electronic load; digital oscilloscope; thermal chamber; function/arbitrary-waveform or control-interface fault generator as needed
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can automate many combined voltage/load/temperature cases; command corruption and narrow control-pin glitches need additional interface or waveform-generation hardware.
Main reference: ISO 26262-5:2018 expanded functional testing; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-010

Test: 12-volt-network overvoltage from 48-volt or high-voltage converter faults
Purpose / failure mechanism: For 48-volt-to-12-volt and high-voltage-to-low-voltage converters, verify that internal faults cannot expose the 12-volt vehicle network to an unsafe source voltage
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject or emulate high-side switch short/power-stage bypass and cross-voltage faults; for isolated converters combine with insulation-failure evidence; verify disconnection or clamping and reaction time
Measure / record: 12-volt-network peak voltage, duration, protection current/energy, diagnostic response and isolation/disconnection time
Acceptance / target: Network voltage and exposure duration remain within the limits allocated by the safety concept, or the fault is isolated within the allocated fault-tolerant time interval
Equipment required: Dedicated 48-volt or high-voltage source with suitable current/energy control; protected cross-fault injection fixture; high-voltage differential probes; digital oscilloscope; Keysight N6700 bench for low-voltage-side loading/monitoring where ratings permit
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A can source up to 60 volts within 5 amperes/300 watts and can support limited 48-volt screening, but it is not a protected high-energy cross-fault/high-voltage safety system; dedicated fault equipment is required.
Main reference: ISO 26262-9:2018 dependent failures; ISO 21780 / ISO 6469-3 context as applicable; see iso26262-asil-test-mapping.md FUSA-011

Test: Protection coordination and selectivity with the vehicle-side fuse
Purpose / failure mechanism: PS-014 and PS-015 characterise the converter's own limits in isolation. They do not establish whether the converter protects before or after the upstream vehicle fuse. Miscoordination means a field fault opens a fuse the service network cannot reset, instead of triggering a recoverable converter shutdown
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject the fault set of PS-015, PS-030 and PS-018 through the representative harness and the actual vehicle-side fuse; repeat at temperature corners
Measure / record: Fault current against time; I²t delivered to the fuse; converter protection trip time; whether the fuse opened; final recoverable state
Acceptance / target: Coordination matches the intended strategy at every fault type and temperature corner; no unintended fuse operation for faults the converter is supposed to clear
Equipment required: Representative fuse and harness; wide-bandwidth current measurement; the existing oscilloscope; sacrificial fuses
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A powers the input through the fuse under test while N6791A and the short-circuit fixture create the fault. Within module ratings this is largely executable on the present bench
Main reference: ISO 8820 fuse series; vehicle-manufacturer harness protection concept; extends PS-014, PS-015, PS-018 and PS-030

Test: Non-volatile memory and reflash integrity during supply interruption
Purpose / failure mechanism: AUTO-009 records non-volatile memory status but nothing deliberately interrupts the supply during a flash write or an over-the-air reflash. A write interrupted mid-sector can corrupt calibration, configuration or safety parameters in a way that survives the next power cycle and never appears as an electrical failure
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject interruptions of the AUTO-010 duration set at randomised phases during non-volatile memory writes and during a full reflash; repeat across the brownout band mapped by AUTO-009; high repetition count
Measure / record: Post-interruption non-volatile memory integrity; checksum/CRC status; bootloader recovery path; diagnostic trouble codes; whether the unit remains field-recoverable
Acceptance / target: No undetected corruption. Every interruption ends in a defined state: valid image, or detected-invalid with a working recovery path
Equipment required: Fast MOSFET interruption fixture with randomised phase control; device under test diagnostic interface; automation for high repetition counts
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A supplies; the deterministic fast fault-injection controller described in the bench automation document is required for sub-millisecond phase control. Stream to the control computer for long campaigns
Main reference: Product requirement; internal safety analysis; extends AUTO-009 and AUTO-010

Test: Quiescent current with bus activity and partial-network wake
Purpose / failure mechanism: AUTO-015 measures sleep current in a quiet state. Real key-off current is dominated by periodic bus wake events and partial-networking frames, so a unit that meets the static budget can still exceed the daily energy budget
Typical stimulus / conditions: Measure over a representative key-off period with realistic bus traffic and partial-networking wake patterns, across voltage and temperature; integrate energy rather than sampling current
Measure / record: Current profile over time; wake-event count and duration; integrated charge and energy per day
Acceptance / target: Vehicle-manufacturer daily energy budget met with realistic bus activity, not only static sleep current
Equipment required: Bus interface and traffic generator; high-dynamic-range current measurement with wide bandwidth and long record; control computer
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A supplies, but its 3 mA current resolution cannot resolve microamp sleep floors or fast wake spikes. A dynamic-range-capable instrument is required, as for AUTO-015
Main reference: LV 124 E-19; vehicle-manufacturer closed-circuit current budget; extends AUTO-015 and PS-006

Test: Power-flow direction change and mode transition
Purpose / failure mechanism: 48V-001 and FUSA-011 assume unidirectional flow. In a bidirectional 48 V↔12 V unit the transition itself is the hazard: dead-time errors, control-mode handover and reverse-recovery stress occur only during direction change and are invisible to every steady-state test
Typical stimulus / conditions: Command direction changes at every combination of source voltage, load and temperature, including commanded reversal during a load transient and during a supply disturbance; include repeated fast reversals
Measure / record: Transition time; excursion on both rails during handover; shoot-through or cross-conduction current; switch voltage stress during reversal; mode-flag consistency
Acceptance / target: No rail excursion outside requirement on either side; no cross-conduction; deterministic transition timing at every corner
Equipment required: Second source on the opposite side; bidirectional or four-quadrant capability; the existing oscilloscope; high-bandwidth current probing
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6791A sinks but cannot source, so it cannot emulate the opposite-side battery. A second source or four-quadrant instrument is required
Main reference: Product requirement; ISO 21780:2020 functional-status framework; applies only to bidirectional converters

Test: Dual-source arbitration and inter-net fault propagation
Purpose / failure mechanism: With both nets energised the unit must decide which side sources, and must not let a fault on one net propagate to the other. Extends AUTO-018 to the case where both sides are independently powered and either can fail
Typical stimulus / conditions: Energise both nets at independent voltages including out-of-range and 0 V; inject the fault set of PS-030 and FUSA-011 on each side in turn; include loss of one net during power transfer
Measure / record: Current between nets; unintended powering; voltage excursion on the healthy net during a fault on the faulted net; isolation action and timing
Acceptance / target: Within the allowed inter-net current; a fault on one net never drives the other outside its requirement
Equipment required: Two independent sources; ammeters on both sides; fault-injection fixture
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: Requires a second independent source in addition to the N6775A, plus current measurement on both nets
Main reference: Extends AUTO-018 and FUSA-011; ISO 21780:2020; internal safety analysis

Test: Mission-profile-based robustness validation and margin mapping
Purpose / failure mechanism: LIFE-005 is the only row that measures margin rather than compliance. Without a mission profile the durations in LIFE-001 and LIFE-004 and the cycle counts in TH-005 have no derivation, and a pass says nothing about how much margin exists
Typical stimulus / conditions: Build the mission profile (temperature collective, voltage collective, cycles, operating hours, humidity, vibration over life); derive the knowledge matrix of dominant failure mechanisms; stress representative samples to failure on each; map the distance between specification limit, first functional failure and destructive failure
Measure / record: Mission profile document; failure-mechanism matrix; measured margin per mechanism; identification of the limiting mechanism
Acceptance / target: Every dominant mechanism has quantified margin against the mission profile. A test-to-pass result with no margin figure does not close this row
Equipment required: The present bench covers the electrical and thermal mechanisms; mechanical, humidity and component mechanisms need the corresponding facilities
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: The N6700 bench plus chamber already supports step-stress on the electrical and thermal mechanisms. This row is mainly planning and analysis work that redirects existing tests
Main reference: SAE J1211:2012 / ZVEI Robustness Validation Handbook; SAE J1879 for semiconductors; frames LIFE-005 and the combined-corner campaign

Test: Component qualification grade against mission profile
Purpose / failure mechanism: PS-029 verifies derating against datasheet limits but nothing checks that the parts are qualified for the location. A Grade 1 IC in a Grade 0 location, or an industrial-grade multilayer ceramic capacitor substituted for an automotive-grade part with the same value and case size, passes every bench test in this matrix and fails in the field
Typical stimulus / conditions: Review the bill of materials against the AEC qualification evidence: grade against the mission-profile temperature; qualification family against the actual part number and dielectric; whether short-circuit reliability data exists for smart power devices in the protection path
Measure / record: Per-part grade, qualification family and evidence reference; exceptions list with rationale; gaps against the mission profile
Acceptance / target: Every part qualified to a grade covering its mission-profile conditions, or a documented and accepted exception
Equipment required: Document review; no bench equipment
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: No bench role. A documentation verification that feeds PS-029, LIFE-004 and the FMEDA behind FUSA-006
Main reference: AEC-Q100 Rev J; AEC-Q101 and AEC-Q101-006; AEC-Q200 Rev E; AEC-Q104; feeds PS-029 and FUSA-006
